lede: Every column in Spark has a type, and some columns hold more than one value: a group of named fields, or a list. Knowing the types, and writing a schema in code, lets you read nested data like a clinic's visit records without guessing.
objectives: Name Spark's common types and the Python values that go with them
Write a schema in code with `StructType` and `StructField`, including nested fields
Read the fields of a struct column with `"vitals.heart_rate"` or `F.col("vitals")["heart_rate"]`
Pick items out of an array column by position and count them with `F.size`

blocks.md:
The `encounters` table above has one row per visit to a clinic. On this page it's loaded as a DataFrame called `encounters`, and `F` is `pyspark.sql.functions`.

Two of its columns aren't plain values. `vitals` is a **struct**: a small group of named fields (heart rate, blood pressure, temperature) stored together in one column. `diagnosis_codes` is an **array**: a list of codes, as many as the visit needed. `printSchema()` shows the fields of each.

blocks.title: A schema with nested columns
blocks.note: `vitals` lists its four fields, indented under it. `diagnosis_codes` is an array whose items (`element`) are strings. In `dtypes` the same types are written on one line, the way you'd write them in a schema string.

blocks.md:
Each type has a name for schema strings, a class in `pyspark.sql.types`, and a kind of Python value that goes in it:

- `STRING`: `StringType()`, a `str`
- `INT` and `BIGINT`: `IntegerType()` and `LongType()`, an `int`
- `DOUBLE`: `DoubleType()`, a `float`
- `DECIMAL(10,2)`: `DecimalType(10, 2)`, a `Decimal`
- `BOOLEAN`: `BooleanType()`, `True` or `False`
- `DATE` and `TIMESTAMP`: `DateType()` and `TimestampType()`, a `date` or `datetime`
- `ARRAY<STRING>`: `ArrayType(StringType())`, a `list`
- `STRUCT<heart_rate: INT>`: `StructType([...])`, a `tuple`, `dict` or `Row`

A whole schema is a `StructType` too: a list of `StructField(name, type, nullable)`, one per column. The third argument says whether the column may be missing; it's `True` unless you say otherwise.

blocks.title: Write a schema in code
blocks.code:
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType, DoubleType, ArrayType

schema = StructType([
    StructField("encounter_id", StringType(), False),
    StructField("vitals", StructType([
        StructField("heart_rate", IntegerType()),
        StructField("temperature_c", DoubleType()),
    ])),
    StructField("diagnosis_codes", ArrayType(StringType())),
])

rows = [("T1", (88, 36.9), ["J06.9"]), ("T2", None, ["Z00.00", "E78.5"])]
visits = spark.createDataFrame(rows, schema)
visits.show()
visits.printSchema()
print(visits.schema.simpleString())
blocks.note: A struct value is a tuple with one item per field, and an array is a Python list. `T2` has no vitals at all, so the whole struct is `None`. `simpleString()` prints the same schema as one string, which `createDataFrame` would accept too.

blocks.title: A missing value in a column that may not be missing
blocks.code:
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType

schema = StructType([StructField("encounter_id", StringType(), False)])
spark.createDataFrame([("T1",), (None,)], schema)
blocks.note: `encounter_id` was declared with `nullable` set to `False`, so Spark refuses a row where it's `None`, and names the field.

blocks.md:
To read one field of a struct, write the column and the field with a dot, `"vitals.heart_rate"`, or pick it out with brackets, `F.col("vitals")["heart_rate"]`. The dot form names the result after the field; the bracket form names it `vitals.heart_rate`, so give it an `alias`. `"vitals.*"` takes every field at once.

When the whole struct is missing, every field read from it is missing too.

blocks.title: Read fields of a struct
blocks.code:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

encounters.select("encounter_id", "vitals.heart_rate", F.col("vitals")["systolic"].alias("systolic")).show()

encounters.select("encounter_id", "vitals.*").show(3)
blocks.note: The last two visits were by video, so they have no vitals and their fields are `NULL`. `vitals.*` turns the four fields into four columns.

blocks.md: An array's items are numbered from **0**. `F.col("diagnosis_codes")[0]` is the first code. `F.size("diagnosis_codes")` counts the items. Asking for a position past the end of an array stops with an error in Spark 4, so only pick positions every row has.

blocks.title: Pick items from an array
blocks.code:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

encounters.select(
    "encounter_id",
    "diagnosis_codes",
    F.col("diagnosis_codes")[0].alias("first_code"),
    F.size("diagnosis_codes").alias("code_count"),
).show(truncate=False)
blocks.note: Every visit has at least one code, so position 0 is always there. `reason` in the table describes that first code.

concept.prompt: A row of `encounters` has `diagnosis_codes` `["J45.909", "E78.5", "J06.9"]`. What is `F.col("diagnosis_codes")[1]` for it?
concept.why: Array positions start at 0, so position 1 is the second code.

concept.prompt: A video visit has no vitals: the whole `vitals` value is missing. What does `"vitals.heart_rate"` give for that row?
choices: An error, because the struct is missing
The heart rate of the previous row
concept.why: When a struct is missing, every field read from it is missing too. No error is raised.

concept.prompt: Which schema string matches `StructType([StructField("heart_rate", IntegerType()), StructField("codes", ArrayType(StringType()))])`?

review: Every column has a type. A struct holds named fields in one column; an array holds a list of values of one type.
A schema in code is a `StructType` of `StructField(name, type, nullable)`. It can nest a `StructType` or an `ArrayType`.
A struct value is a tuple (or dict or `Row`) and an array value is a Python list. A missing struct is `None`.
Read a struct field with `"vitals.heart_rate"` or `F.col("vitals")["heart_rate"]`; `"vitals.*"` takes every field.
Array items start at position 0, and `F.size` counts them. A position past the end is an error.
Fields read from a missing struct are missing too.
